entry.note: caller-supplied revision string; rev_parse(str(rev) + '^0') hands the name before '^' to name_to_object, which tries it as a ref path with the bare '%s' template first

guards.note: applied at the top of _get_ref_info_helper; rejects ref names starting with '/', containing '..' or '//', backslashes, colons, control characters etc., so an absolute name raises ValueError before any join/open

sinks.note: open(os.path.join(repodir, str(ref_path))); an absolute ref_path makes os.path.join discard repodir, so any file outside the git dir is opened and read (the regressed side only rejects '..')

notes: Pilot spec, re-reviewed at 2.3 on 2026-09-29 (flow kept; Repo.head added to the slice, notes rewritten). Second half of a two-part fix. 74e55ee4 (PR #1644, 3.1.35) added an inline '..' check in _get_ref_info_helper; it is already present at the regressed commit 1774f1e3 (first parent of the merge e98f57b8, PR #1672, 3.1.37), so the advisory's '../' PoC is blocked on BOTH sides of this pair and does not distinguish them. The flow this pair closes is the absolute-path variant: Repo.commit('/etc/passwd') -> self.rev_parse('/etc/passwd^0') (class alias of git/repo/fun.py::rev_parse, imported from .fun) -> the name before the first '^' goes to name_to_object('/etc/passwd') -> the bare '%s' template -> SymbolicReference.dereference_recursive -> _get_ref_info -> _get_ref_info_helper -> open(os.path.join(repodir, '/etc/passwd')), where os.path.join discards repodir (repo.common_dir via _git_dir) for an absolute ref_path and the file is opened and read in full. The regressed side only rejects names containing '..'. The clean side calls _check_ref_name_valid (git-check-ref-format rules) first; it rejects a leading '/', and '//' for the 'refs/%s'-style templates, so every template raises ValueError, name_to_object ends in BadName, and nothing outside the git dir is opened. Verified 2026-09-29 by running the complete git/ package extracted from each commit (only the external gitdb/smmap stubbed) against a real temporary repository, calling Repo.commit with an audit hook logging every open(): at 1774f1e3 an absolute rev opened the marker file outside .git (and a nonexistent absolute path was probed the same way); at e98f57b8 the same revs opened nothing; '../x' was rejected with no open at both; 'master' produced the same in-.git opens at both. Platform detail: rev_parse splits the rev at any of '^~:@', so a Windows drive-letter path ('C:\...') or a path containing '~' (8.3 short names) is truncated before name_to_object; a POSIX absolute path, or a drive-relative '/Users/...' path on Windows (the case verified above), reaches open() intact. Impact is a blind read (existence probe, DoS on /dev/random or a huge file); contents are not returned, except that a file beginning 'ref: X' is followed as a ref and one beginning with a 40-hex token is treated as a sha. Parallel entry points not modelled: Repo.tree (rev + '^{tree}') and IndexFile.diff reach the same rev_parse path; they are left out for size (the clean slice is 24,576 bytes, exactly the soft limit). Repo.common_dir (the source of repodir) is not in the slice; it does not matter for this variant because os.path.join discards repodir for an absolute ref_path. Repo.head was added (a 3-line property) so Repo.commit's rev-is-None branch and rev_parse's leading-token branch resolve in the slice; neither reaches the sink. Slice artefact: class-level assignments kept by the builder reference cut methods (Repo.description/refs/branches/daemon_export/alternates, SymbolicReference.commit/object/reference), so the slice files are not importable as-is; unrelated to the flow. Repo keeps its class-level unsafe_git_clone_options list (real identifier and values; the builder keeps all class-level assignments); it belongs to clone option checking, not to this flow.
